title: The explanatory power of signed jumps for the risk-return tradeoff
summary: Signed jumps add limited predictive information in the inspected source; no new strategy or return trial.
about: Whether signed intraday jumps improve S&P futures risk-return forecasts.
findings: Authors find limited incremental information from signed jumps; continuous risk supplies most explanatory power in1996–July2008 data.
mechanism: Compensation for conditional market risk is proposed; predictive association is not a costed trading payoff.
build_on: No current TEST. Minute prices can support raw realized measures, but the inspected result gives weak support for a new incremental net edge.
can_strategy_code_be_made: Feature/regression code is feasible; inventing sign thresholds or trading windows would add a new unsupported rule.
reading_scope: Selected primary18-page PDF introduction, signed-jump equations, data/method and initial results; not entire paper.
owned_input_mapping: Owned ES minute OHLCV is a raw-field overlap, not an authenticated SP futures/control-variable/overnight replication.
deeper_investigation: Deeper strategy development is not warranted from this weak incremental source result. This is distinct from the parked2013 Economic Modelling downside-risk paper.
